I have been farming these 6 mu for 30 years, since I was 20 years old. I never went to school, not even one day. Everything I know, I learned from doing it with my own hands and watching the old farmers around me. My father farmed this land before me, and now my sons help sometimes. We have a well, so when the crops need water, I start the pump. Electricity costs money, so I count every time I turn it on.

For wheat, I do what I did last year, because last year was decent — I got about 500 jin per mu. After the maize comes off in June, I till the stubble with the rotary tiller, then sow the wheat. I buy the improved seeds from the dealer, the same kind my neighbor Lao Wang uses — his wheat always looks thick and strong. At sowing time, I spread base fertilizer: about 80 jin per mu of compound fertilizer, the kind in the bag with numbers on it. Then in the spring, when the wheat wakes up and turns green, I top-dress with urea — about 50 jin per mu. Some people at the market say I use too much, but I saw what happened to Old Zhang three years ago when he cut back: his wheat turned yellow and thin, and he lost half a crop. I would rather waste some fertilizer than lose yield. A bad harvest means my family goes hungry. I irrigate four times: once before winter so the wheat doesn't freeze dry, once when it greens up in March, once at jointing when the stems shoot up, and once when the grain is filling. For spraying, I do herbicide in early spring when the broadleaf weeds come up, then I spray twice more for aphids and rust if the weather gets humid — usually I spray three times total. I expect about 550 kg per mu if the weather is fair.

For maize, right after we cut the wheat in early June, I sow straight into the stubble with the no-till seeder. No point in tilling again — wastes diesel and time, and everyone around here sows maize this way now. I use hybrid seeds, the kind from the seed dealer. You cannot grow maize without hybrid anymore — the old traditional seeds would give you nothing. At sowing, I put down about 60 jin per mu of compound fertilizer in the row. Then when the maize is about knee-high, maybe 20 days later, I side-dress urea — about 60 jin per mu. That's what I did last year and my maize made about 550 jin per mu. I irrigate twice: once right after sowing if the soil is dry, and once when the tassels come out and the ears are filling. If August is very hot, maybe a third time, but usually twice is enough. I spray herbicide right after sowing to kill the weeds, and I spray once more for corn borer when I see moths flying around the field in July. I hope for 600 kg per mu this year.

I watch my costs. A bag of urea is expensive now. But I have a family of four to feed, and any shortfall in yield is a disaster I cannot afford. I look at what Lao Wang does, and what the others on this lane do. We all buy from the same dealer, we all use about the same amounts. If someone tries a new seed and it works on his field for two years, maybe I will try it. But not this year. This year I will do what I know.
